Thanks for the demo this morning — everything was helpful. Two quick clarifying items on our side before we loop in procurement:

- Traffic profile: expected steady-state ~20 req/s with spikes to 60 req/s for ~10 minutes during business hours. Some endpoints will be small (few hundred tokens); others up to ~3k tokens per call.

Thanks Daniel — great questions. Below is a short, practical breakdown to help you decide. I attached a one-page quickstart and an endpoint-slice example CSV for your ops team.

Summary — Hosted API pilot fit? Yes, with caveats
- Hosted pilot is the fastest path: we can provision sandbox endpoints in EU region (Frankfurt) and ensure request processing and logs remain in-region for the pilot window.
- Rate handling: we can map a single model to multiple endpoints and assign per-endpoint rate slices. For your mix (20 steady -> 60 burst), a sandbox with two endpoints (primary 40rps, burst 80rps for short periods) is a common pattern.
- Token profile: prefix/KV caching and batching typically reduce token spend for multi-turn flows; Aditya has an endpoint mapping suggestion below.

When to consider Dedicated/Private
- Dedicated: recommended when you need contractual latency/throughput SLAs or sustained >150 rps. Reserved capacity gives predictable unit economics and burst buffers.
- Private/VPC or on-prem: necessary if you require customer-managed infrastructure, strict egress controls, or legally mandated on-prem processing of model inputs.

Quickstart steps (hosted pilot) — high level
1) Sign-off on TOS and data-residency addendum (1–2 business days).
2) We provision EU-region sandbox endpoints (project + two endpoints) and share sandbox API keys.
3) You run smoke tests and a 3-day traffic soak with pre-agreed slices (we do tail latency monitoring).
4) If results look good, transition to a short-term paid pilot with higher quota and telemetry retention.

Attachments: Redwood_Hosted_Pilot_Quickstart.pdf (step checklist), Endpoint_Slice_Example.csv (sample mapping)

Next steps suggested
- I can have Aditya share a sample endpoint mapping and recommended throttle values by EOD.
- If you want procurement involved now, happy to send a one-page commercial for a pilot.

Would you like us to: (a) provision EU sandbox now, or (b) send the pilot SOW and brief commercial?

Hi Daniel — quick technical notes to complement Marissa's summary:

- Endpoint mapping idea: primary (model-gpt-medium-eu) for conversational traffic (40 rps); aux endpoint (model-gpt-medium-eu-burst) with higher concurrency and relaxed batching to absorb spikes to 80rps.
- Throttles: set soft limits at per-endpoint 40 rps, hard caps at 85 rps. Use 429 backoff with exponential jitter.
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated prompts (e.g., static system messages) reduces compute; KV cache to reduce recompute for long sessions.
- Telemetry: we can provide token-level cost breakdown and tail-latency dashboards during the pilot.

Operational checklist for the sandbox I can spin up today if you confirm EU region and access list (emails) for sandbox keys. I recommend including a simple synthetic traffic test (10–15 minutes at 60 rps) to validate tail behavior.

Attachment: Endpoint_Slice_Example.csv (simple two-row mapping).
